key_insight: The paper proposes an ultrafast, deterministic atom-ion controlled-Z gate using a Rydberg-induced force on the atom and an optical Magnus force on the ion, enabling quantum state transfer between neutral atoms and trapped-ion registers.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical interconnect for hybrid quantum computing architectures, speeding up short-range QCCD links and allowing atom logical qubits to be written into ion-based memory blocks.
method: Use a charge-induced-dipole ($C_4$) interaction between a Rydberg-excited atom and a trapped ion to generate entanglement.
Apply a spin-dependent optical Magnus force on the ion to close phase-space trajectories in a few microseconds.
Toggle the atom’s Rydberg state to extend the approach to multi-ion crystals with negligible overhead.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level Monte Carlo simulations indicate the hybrid architecture can support orders of magnitude more operations than atom-only or ion-only systems at the same code distance and logical error rate.
watch_item: The scheme depends on precise ultrafast control of Rydberg excitation and ion motion, so decoherence, addressing errors, and experimental timing stability may limit real-world performance.
paper_title: Deterministic atom-shuttle interconnects via ultrafast atom-ion entangling gate
